prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one explanatory comparison diagram. Allow only the distinct views, stages or comparison panels explicitly authored in this page's illustration brief, with their exact relationships and counts. No unrequested panels, insets, annotations or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Transport Through Time; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: A selected past-to-present comparison of transport power followed by clearly supervised prototypes for future use. Historical pictures are reconstructions, not one universal worldwide timeline. Plain practical clothing and neutral locations only; no flags, religious/political symbols, brands or named child cast. Past examples: a bay horse with brown wooden wagon, a wooden rowing boat and cream-sailed wooden boat, black steam locomotive with red wheels and brown coaches, early dark-green motor car, blue motor bus and red goods truck, cream propeller biplane. Present examples: white passenger ferry, blue-hulled container ship, white-and-teal passenger jet, white-and-blue electric train, blue battery car, teal electric bus, blue pedal-assist bicycle and orange cargo bicycle. Prototypes: white car with teal trim and mounted camera/roof sensor on closed test track; white-and-orange small electric propeller aircraft in a test hangar. Prototypes have adult supervision; their illustration is not a forecast that this exact design will be adopted.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Bay horse and brown wooden wagon; Wooden rowing boat with two coherent oars; Small wooden sailing boat with cream sail; Black steam locomotive with red wheels and two brown coaches; Early dark-green car, blue bus and red goods truck; White passenger ferry and blue-hulled container ship; Cream biplane and white teal-tail passenger jet; White-blue electric train, blue battery car and teal electric bus; Blue electric bicycle and orange cargo bicycle with empty child seat; White teal-trim camera-and-sensor test car; White-orange small experimental electric propeller aircraft; Closed battery modules, workshop scale, trolley and chargers
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and specific stages explicitly required below; the declared diagram permits no other scenes or story events.
Page 10. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): From muscle and wind to engines and batteries, power has changed vehicles. Future designs must still carry people and goods safely.
Required illustration: Three clearly separated comparison scenes answering the book's progression: LEFT the bay horse pulls the brown wagon along a dirt road; CENTER the teal modern electric bus stands at its depot charger with a properly connected cable; RIGHT the white-and-orange experimental electric aircraft is parked at its test hangar while the same engineer checks a closed battery module on a trolley beside it. Give each scene its own appropriate surface and complete safely framed subjects. Keep the prototype visibly in testing rather than carrying public passengers. This final comparison shows muscle-powered travel, present electric transport, and a design still being developed. No generic park collage, road map, speed race, floating vehicle, text, arrows, flags or logos.
Exact current state: Closing synthesis compares earlier power, current battery power and a tested design: changing the power system does not remove the basic job of carrying people or goods safely.
Do not add events or stages beyond the authored diagram. Repeat a subject only when the authored comparison or cutaway requires it. No written title; the app renders live text.
Render 1536 by 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2. Clean crisp 2D cartoon, no embossed or painted texture. Keep all required subjects fully inside an 8 percent safe margin, with coherent human anatomy and vehicle geometry. This is a finished individual book illustration: never reproduce the reference board or add unrequested subjects/panels. No words, numbers, logos, flags, title or watermark. If several panels are authored, each contains only its exact requested vehicle scene. Future examples are supervised tests, not a claim that they are available for ordinary passenger use.

visualReview.note: Final triptych returns to the same inquiry: horsewagon at left, present electricbus connected to a charger center, and experimental white/orange electricplane with engineer checking closed battery modules at a testhangar right. Test equipment remains in the already-authored testing context; no extra prototypecar or unrelated new transport stage. Appropriate separate surfaces and full principal vehicle silhouettes support earlier/current/still-tested comparison rather than a generic parkcollage.
